paragraphs: Hyman cites Bamidbar Rabbah 15:16 and suggests reading “Rabbi Yehudah HaLevi bar Shalom.”

notes.text: The printed chapter locator פט״ר-טו remains unclear. A bounded lookup at candidate Bamidbar Rabbah16:15 did not establish the named passage, so no16:15 correction is adopted.

The connected passage in saved named Torat Emet Bamidbar Rabbah chapter 14 names Yuda HaLevi bar Shalom. This supports the availability of Hyman’s suggested Yehudah form without locating the exact passage denoted by פט״ר-טו. Hyman’s נראה remains tentative, and the Yehoshua heading is not silently repaired. No new chapter-9, chapter-19 or 16:15 absence claim is made.

Hyman (vol. II, p. 652) prints פט״ו־טז, which points to Bamidbar Rabbah 15:16. The consulted text there names Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi ben Rabbi Shalom in the Ruth and Boaz dialogue. Chapter 14 separately names Rabbi Yuda HaLevi bar Shalom in a teaching about Jericho. Hyman’s proposed Yehudah reading is tentative, and his heading gives Yehoshua HaLevi bar Shalom.
